title: _current_spot_price reads a quarter up to 45 min stale under 15-minute price entries
claim: With 15-minute price entries (what the default Tibber QUARTER_HOURLY pull returns), HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._current_spot_price returns the earliest entry that started within the last hour instead of the entry covering now. It is wrong on 28..42 of 96 quarters per day when prices ramp within the hour, and on 12..18 of 96 when prices are constant within each hour (the three quarters after every price change). The published current_price, the settlement's price/spot_price, sysid's price and the comfort learner's relative price all read it.

evidence.unit: quarters of 96 mispriced per non-flat profile (ramp arm); step arm 12..18; mean |err| 0.042..0.584 per kWh, mean 0.185, leave-max-out 0.105
evidence.machine: B7 audit container, linux
evidence.contention_note: light seat; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: In _current_spot_price, replace the entry span timedelta(hours=1) with 15 minutes (the harness does this in memory with --perturb)
perturbation.observed_value: The quarter-entry arms fall to 0 mismatches and the hourly-entries null control rises from 0 to 273. The span is the mechanism; an honest fix takes each entry's end from the next entry's start, as _known_prices_for does, and must read 0 on all three arms.

metric_definition: Per profile, the count of 96 quarters where _current_spot_price() differs from the entry covering now.
phenomenon_property: Every seam that prices 'now' from the price entry list must use each entry's real span, taken from the entries, and not a fixed one-hour span.
proposed_fix_scope: Make _current_spot_price look up the covering entry the way _known_prices_for does (bisect on the sorted starts; the end is the next start), or call _known_prices_for([now]) directly. Add a features.py pin with quarter entries at :07 past each quarter.
mechanism: Full original metric_definition (moved here by intake normalisation, 219 chars, over the 200-char schema limit): "Per profile, the count of the 96 quarters (clock frozen 7 minutes into each) where _current_spot_price() differs from the price of the entry whose [start, start+15 min) contains now; keyed on the value the seam returns."

title: PV piecewise cost clipped by import_margin's zero floor wherever import price < export price
claim: pv.import_margin floors (import - export) at zero, so wherever import < export on a surplus step, HeatPumpOptimizer._energy_cost_fn and pv.blended_block_prices price surplus-covered energy at the import price instead of the export compensation it forgoes. This breaks the stated identity export·min(P,s)+import·max(P−s,0) on 16 of 96 steps for summer_negative at the shipped default export price 0.0. On a real solve the published predicted_cost is −0.609 where the identity gives 0.000, and the plan draws 5.07 kWh from surplus in negative-price steps against 2.27 kWh unfloored.

evidence.unit: steps of 96 breaching the piecewise identity (summer_negative, export 0.0 default); summer_typical @0.30 = 20; signed error per day at 3 kW, export 0.30: range −5.04..0, mean −1.14, leave-most-negative-out −0.36; solve predicted_cost − identity = −0.609
evidence.machine: B7 audit container, linux
evidence.contention_note: light seat; counts and currency identities are contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: exact for counts; ±1e-6 for the solve's currency figure

perturbation.change: Remove the zero floor in pv.import_margin, returning import − export unclipped (the harness does this in memory with --perturb via mock.patch.object)
perturbation.observed_value: Breach steps fall to 0 in every cell, the solve's predicted_cost − identity goes from −0.609 to 0.000, and surplus kWh in negative-price steps goes from 5.07 to 2.27.

metric_definition: Per (price profile, export price) cell, count of 96 steps where the production cost closure's price of a single-step draw differs from the export/import identity.
phenomenon_property: Every PV-aware pricing seam must charge surplus-covered energy at the export compensation for any sign of import − export; no seam may floor the margin.
proposed_fix_scope: Drop the clip in pv.import_margin, or replace it with a guard only on non-finite values. Correct its docstring's rationale: with export > import, the unfloored cost is still correct and does not invert anything. Add a features.py pin covering a negative-import surplus step and an export > import step through both _energy_cost_fn and blended_block_prices.
mechanism: Full original metric_definition (moved here by intake normalisation, 273 chars, over the 200-char schema limit): "Per (price profile, export price) cell, the count of the 96 steps where the production cost closure's price of a 3 kW single-step draw differs by more than 1e-9 from export·min(P,s)+import·max(P−s,0)·dt with a clear-sky 6 kWp surplus; keyed on the closure's returned value."

title: sysid two-state fit rolls the candidate one Euler step per sample: UA 17-25% low, 0/3 presets adopt

Full original title (moved here by intake normalisation, 140 chars, over the 120-char schema limit): "sysid two-state fit rolls the candidate with one Euler step per 30-min sample: UA 17-25% low on an exact continuous plant, 0/3 presets adopt"

title: On an on/off pump, the switch path switches off steps whose planned heat the plan books as delivered
claim: The solver treats a step below the modulation floor as duty cycling within the step (bounds [0,P_max], optimizer.py ~:3962). On an on/off pump (min==max==6 kW, which config_flow._power_errors accepts) the threshold is 3 kW, so the plan's 1.0-1.4 kW trickle is switched OFF while the trajectory, cost and savings count that heat as delivered. On/off arm: 4/9 cells withhold more than 10% of planned energy. Shoulder withholds 0.671 (8.30 of 12.38 kWh over 30 steps), producing 30 end-to-end switch.turn_off calls on steps with planned heat. Modulating null arm: 0/9 cells (max 0.014) and 0 such calls. Shoulder open-loop consequence: min room 20.64 C planned vs 19.89 C actuated, 17.2 K*h below the plan's own trajectory, 0 K*h below min_temperature.

title: On an on/off pump every full-power step publishes as 'eco' and power_normalized runs to -60
claim: get_current_action computes p_norm = (P - min)/max(max - min, 0.1). When min==max the 0.1 kW divisor floor turns a degenerate range into a x10 scale. A full-power 6 kW step gets p_norm 0, so HeatPumpActionSensor.native_value is 'eco' rather than 'boost', and idle steps publish power_normalized = -60. On/off arm: 149 full-power steps mislabelled across 7/9 cells (range 0-31, LOO 118); power_normalized minimum -60.0. Modulating null arm: 0 mislabelled; minimum -0.2, which is the same formula on every install and goes as a lead. The climate hvac_action is unaffected because it also reads heat_pump_on.

title: A report-on-change indoor thermometer silent over 60 min turns Indoor Temperature unavailable
claim: With the indoor thermometer's state '21.3' valid in Home Assistant but last reported 61, 90, 240 or 480 min ago, the integration's Indoor Temperature sensor is unavailable in 4 of 7 silence cells (available at 5-59 min), and a thermometer that re-writes an unchanged value (last_reported 5 min, last_updated 480 min) stays available, so the gaps come from genuine report silence, not from ignoring last_reported. Full original title (moved here by intake normalisation, 126 chars, over the 120-char schema limit): "A report-on-change indoor thermometer silent over 60 min turns Indoor Temperature unavailable while HA holds its valid reading"
mechanism: InputReader._age_gate marks the indoor reading stale once its last_reported/last_updated age exceeds INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[indoor] = 60 min (x staleness scale, default 1.0); reading_ok['upper_floor_temperature'] goes False and _MeasuredTemperatureMixin.available follows it. A thermometer that reports only on change (common for battery Zigbee/BLE sensors: a stable room for hours sends nothing and Home Assistant writes nothing) therefore reads as dead, contradicting const.py's stated intent that the limits are 'generous multiples of a normal reporting interval so that a healthy sensor never trips them'. The user sees history gaps (reported: ~16:30-20:45 and ~03:30-06:15 local, the stable hours); the same stale flag also withholds the reading from the cycle. D1-s5-01's age_of seam (inlet/humidity) ignores last_reported, but this path does not: its re-report arm is available.

phenomenon_property: A measured input whose source entity still holds a valid state in Home Assistant is not published as unavailable merely because a healthy report-on-change device sent nothing for an hour; staleness of such inputs is judged by the source's own availability or a limit its reporting pattern cannot trip. Too-eager question (orchestrator addendum): the guard is too eager exactly for report-on-change thermometers silent over 60 min (4 of 7 cells, every silence >= 61 min); an unchanged value that moves only last_reported does NOT trip it (rereport_unavailable=0 of 1).
